zpl_vec4_mag2 needs to ensure its return value is finite, which depends on zpl_vec4_dot returning a finite value.

data.rationale: zpl_vec4_mag2 calls zpl_vec4_dot(v,v) with identical arguments. The squared magnitude is always non-negative, so when both arguments are the same vector, the dot product (sum of squares) must be >= 0.
zpl_vec4_dot is a pure computation with no side effects - it takes structs by value and returns a scalar.

Cannot provide this postcondition. zpl_vec3_dot is a general dot product of two vectors v0 and v1. The requested property (v0.x != 0 || v0.y != 0 || v0.z != 0) ==> result > 0 only holds when v0 == v1 (self dot product), but the function signature allows arbitrary v0 and v1. For example, dot(v, -v) = -|v|^2 < 0. The caller zpl_vec3_norm calls dot(v, v) and should rely on the exact value postcondition: ensures \result == \add_float(\add_float(\mul_float(v0.x, v1.x), \mul_float(v0.y, v1.y)), \mul_float(v0.z, v1.z)); When the caller knows v0 == v1, it can deduce the result equals v.x*v.x + v.y*v.y + v.z*v.z which is >= 0, and > 0 when any component is non-zero.
